title: How political candidates view security - NewsBreak
text:
By Tom Hanson ,
58 minutes ago SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (KELO) — In the wake of the Charlie Kirk shooting and the assassination of a Minnesota lawmaker and her husband, do political candidates here at home and in Washington need to think about security? It’s a question we posed to the people running for South Dakota Governor.
Candidate Toby Doeden, who reported to police that he was threatened by a woman at a Northern State Football game last week, says it’s a sad day that we even have to discuss security.
Story continues below
“We’re taking a hard look at getting some security. I’ve got hundreds and hundreds of employees, I’ve got an amazing family, and my second grandchild was born 48 hours ago. I have a lot of people that count on me, so I’m going to do everything that I can to protect myself, but it is a sad day that we are here, a very sad day,” said Doeden.
Robert Arnold, the 20-year-old Democrat from Pierre running for Governor, told us quote.
“We need to call out the people who made this hostile environment.” And “I’m not worried, the people showing up to my rallies, they’re not the type of people who are violent.
Republican candidate Jon Hanson sent us a statement, which in part says
“Having been the recipient of death threats and wishes of harm to me because of my conservative values, it’s not something I take lightly.” He also said, “People should be able to speak their minds without fear of violence.”
Independent candidate for Governor Terry Gleason, who says he considers himself a conservative independent, told us, quote.
“As soon as we formally announce, we should have some protections. It is scary for us candidates because we are not elected officials yet. He also said, “I personally do feel safe because I’m an independent, not in party conflict.”
Congressman Dusty Johnson, who is in Washington, was asked if members of Congress need more security.
“Clearly, what happened to Charlie Kirk is an absolute tragedy. I do think the toxicity in this country it’s not just a problem for member security, it’s a problem for us getting anything done. And clearly, we need to address some root causes. Why are Americans so angry? What are politicians and influencers doing to make things worse? And how can we stop that doom cycle?” said Johnson.
